reason: Batch of independently reviewed PRs, each green on its own: #999: Regression coverage for the fresh-Core first-chat HTTP 500 that #1000 fixed on main (the #987 retirement guard's UPDATE on project_ownership inside execution workers). This PR now adds tests only: an execution worker creates and unarchives owned chats without changing its ownership row, a retirement hold rejects worker chat create and unarchive, a retirement racing an uncommitted worker chat start waits and keeps the worker, and a real Core built from source streams the first chat of a new project through its admitted worker. The existing #1000 execution chat-start case is selected alongside them. #1044: Test-only repair of Butler suites left red on main after the async storage conversion (#939, 831d0d0) and the 60% compaction target (6509bd4). The tests now await Core's async Butler, work, goal, queue, settings, workspace and automation-policy APIs; helpers, stubs and listeners Core now awaits are async; asyncio.run inside the running loop is replaced with await; a fabricated active harness entry is removed before teardown shutdown; setup tests read status once before refreshing because the fixture skips the lifespan that starts detection; the recovery matrix gives its local model a configured context window. Selected: every test in the 11 fully green touched files and the passing node ids in test_butler_host_load and test_butler_setup_controls, plus test_butler_authority.py, test_butler_tool_failures.py and test_butler_resources.py as whole files: #1039 (67018d4, with the butler_authority product fix) and #1011 (2d0f7ce) already repaired those three files on main, so this branch leaves them identical to main and selects them to show they stay green beside these repairs. No product code changed. #1065: #939 made NotebookService.policy, AutomationRuntimeManager.update_project_policy and WorkspaceService.download async but two Butler actions still called them without await. nebula.settings.set_notebook raised AttributeError ('coroutine' object has no attribute execution_mode/approval_policy/host_access_acknowledged) on every mode or network change and saved nothing; its policy update was also un-awaited, and a mode change never called finish_policy_change, so a prepared change left the project's notebook admission paused ('Project mode is changing') until Core restarted. nebula.data.create_starter_files wrote the templates, then its read-back crashed ('coroutine' object has no attribute 'stream'), so Butler reported a failure and a retry was refused. The fix awaits all three calls, releases the mode change in a finally block like the Project settings route, and awaits the download on the loop with only the stream read in a thread. Selected: two new Butler set_notebook regressions over a real NotebookService and AutomationRuntimeManager (both fail on main), the Butler administration suite (its two starter-template cases are this defect's regression and fail on main), the other Butler notebook cases that pass on main, the guides starter-files route, the Settings API policy suite (the Project settings automation-policy route the fix mirrors) and the settings-assistant tool cases that pass on main. #1066: Composer text typed while the page re-keys or resizes was lost. CI run 43618511390 (webkit-430, host-load.spec.ts) is WebKit dropping keystrokes after SelectionActionsProvider cleared the document selection on a window resize while the composer had focus (the selection is the caret); the draft key change also dropped text on a Core reconnect (new client and temporary scope), after a first send named its chat, and after a failed first send gave it up. Selected: chatDraftStorage.test.ts (the new draftFollowsKeyChange rules: same chat through a temporary scope, never across two Core identities, only the chat this composer named or gave up, never another project) and the existing draft storage cases; selectionActions.test.tsx (a resize keeps a focused text box's caret and still clears a page selection elsewhere) and the existing selection cases; chatFollowUpStorage.test.ts (follow-up storage shares the draft key); the new mocked-Core stabilization journey on desktop, Chromium phone and WebKit 320/390/430 (types through a resize and an identity-less Core reconnect; fails on main in Chromium at the reconnect and in WebKit at the resize); and the playwright-impact manifest checks that pass on main, since the catalog gained an area. #1068: Worker-backed GUI panes stayed in error after an idle project's worker retired and was readmitted, until a reload. Core now answers project reads without a ready worker with a coded, retryable 503 (project_runtime_unavailable + reason starting/closing/idle, Retry-After: 1) and the UI waits for the runtime instead of failing: one shared probe, every pane re-reads in place, one calm status line. Selected: test_api_worker.py (the coded 503 for each reason and the unchanged body for other private-channel failures, plus the existing API-worker contract), test_runtime_routing.py (the new idle/starting/closing reasons and the existing routing cases), test_runtime_http.py (the proxy codes only project reads; the host channel keeps its body), test_execution_worker.py except the flaky idle-probe case (a starting worker's coded 503, failed/fenced gates, the existing worker lifecycle), the playwright-impact manifest checks that pass on main (the catalog gained an area), the new and changed vitest suites for the recovery module, client, panes, workspace collections and subagents, plus existing suites around the changed client send path and app shell, and the new real-Core journey on desktop, Chromium 390 and WebKit 390. The journey now sets the fixture's idle grace to 0 (a test-fixture control only): since #1062 a quiet project's worker stays 300 s after its last command, and the journey's archive is such a command. #1069: DeploymentCoordinator.target_execution and rollback_code ignored _compatible's False result for a third resident execution version (MAX_EXECUTION_VERSIONS = 2), so deployment_host.target_version could name a release reserve_worker always refuses. Automatic admission and expired-owner recovery start workers only at the target: a new project's chat stayed queued without a worker while every 0.5 s pass re-verified the bundle and bumped the host revision. Both operations now raise OperationRejected (definite failed receipt, operator-readable reason) and change nothing; the staged deployer checks resident_versions before the target step, keeps the API promotion and returns api_promoted_execution_staged, and resumes once a slot frees. Selected: the staged deployer suite (fake host now refuses like Core; updated third-version test plus resume and rollback regressions), the host-activation deployer suite, the deployment lifecycle suite (new coordinator regression on SQLite and PostgreSQL), the admission retry cases including the new admission regression, the auto-recovery suite (reads the target), the shutdown readmission cases whose fixture targets execution, the reserve_worker third-version refusal process case, and execution/API feature compatibility. #1058: The terminal /board was read-only while the GUI's Work page creates items, checks in, tracks or links a conversation and toggles agent Work tools. The board now performs those actions with Core readback (N new Ready item; U check-in with summary/next step/blocker/status; T track this conversation as an In Progress linked item, following the GUI's request-ID chain (track:<chat>:after:<done item>, at most 50 steps) past items Core returns as Done; L link the selected item, sending its revision and refusing another chat's item; A agent Work tools with the project revision), with inline prompts where Escape cancels without a write, and /board new|update|track|link|tools in the plain terminal. Selected: the board unit suites (existing and new actions with an in-memory Work Core applying Core's rules), TUI and shell suites for the footer and command text, the client wheel allowlist, the existing board real-Core journey and a new installed-wheel PTY journey on a paired TLS LAN Core, the product-knowledge search and Chroma digest sync, and the settings-catalog terminal test. #1067: Re-tracking a conversation after its tracked Work item is Done was a silent no-op: the Work page's Track posted request_id 'track:<session>' (a key per conversation) and Core returns a request ID's first item whatever its status, so Track returned the Done item, ignored the new title and the conversation still had no open item. Track now follows a deterministic chain: while Core returns a Done item it posts again with 'track:<session>:after:<done item id>' (at most 50 steps), so repeated clicks, other tabs and other clients reach the same open item and a finished item is never reused. Core's retry contract is unchanged (Work import reuses request IDs for Done items). Selected: WorkPage.test.tsx (its mock POST now follows Core's request-ID rule; the new re-track case fails on main; also covers another client tracking first) and the work-import real-Core browser journey, extended to finish the tracked item with a check-in and track the conversation again (one Done and one new In progress item, the Working-now link opens the new one). That spec was red on main and is repaired: 32+ character token (minimum since 2d9f099), Idempotency-Key on its API mutations (required since b833782), a readiness wait before the first mutation, and removal of Core's read-only retained release; the helpers are in the new shared ui/tests/fixtures/core-api.ts. #1071: Every provider chat goal that used up its step budget left WARNING chat.goal.auto_continue_failed ('A running conversation goal could not start its next turn', ChatConfigurationError 'goal step budget is exhausted.') although the goal ended correctly (Paused, 'Goal step budget is exhausted.'). prepare_async's budget check pauses the goal with the precise reason and raises; the goal continuation's broad except recorded that as a failure. The same happened for the active-time budget, the token paths that pause inside prepare (cannot fit the next request, exhausted during context compaction) and the subagent-report continuation (chat.subagent.goal_continue_failed). Those budget pauses now raise GoalBudgetConfigurationError (a ChatConfigurationError subclass, so 422 mapping, WARNING/invalid_input classification and existing pytest.raises checks are unchanged), which both continuations treat as diagnostic-expected; every other configuration failure is still recorded and still pauses the goal. Selected: the whole goal suite test_chat_goals.py, whose provider auto-continue test now asserts no chat.goal.auto_continue_failed record when the step budget is reached (fails on main), and the subagent lifecycle tests by name. #1073: API and execution workers exited on the first failed heartbeat when PostgreSQL refused or reset connections, though their 30 s leases were still valid; the execution lease watcher fenced the project on any SQL error (wedging it if the heartbeat kept renewing), each streamed chat frame failed on the first lost connection, and the memory reconciler and chat schedule loop died on one failed read. Workers now keep a local monotonic lease bound (LeaseRenewal: last acknowledged renewal start + LEASE_MS - LEASE_SAFETY_MS); inside it the heartbeat retries transient SQL errors (runtime_worker.keep_lease), worker sessions wait to bind a connection before any statement (Database.ride_out_outages, opt-in), the watcher and prepared-restoration wait do not fence, and stream publication retries under the same batch key; past the bound the worker stops with LeaseLost as before, and a definite LeaseLost or SQL answer still stops it at once. Selected: the new outage suite (keeper bound, session wait, real heartbeat on SQLite/PostgreSQL that never resurrects an expired lease); the execution worker suite with the new watcher regression; the worker features suite with the in-process run_worker regression; the memory recovery suite with the loop regression; the journal retry regression and the chat stream cases that pass on main; the coordination, async database/PostgreSQL/auxiliary database, API worker composition, write-lock, runtime memory recovery and diagnostic boundary suites that exercise Database.session, heartbeats and the lease watcher. #1075: An operator's Stop (or Resume) of assistant browser control could answer 409 'revision conflict' and leave the Assistant in control: BrowserCompanion.takeover saved assistant_paused with the revision it had just read, while the viewer's 3 s tab poll rewrote the same BrowserSession row on every call and a reconnect wrote it too; the viewer only showed the storage error in its generic notice. Core writers of that row now apply their own fields to the row as stored and retry when another writer saved first, the tab poll writes nothing when nothing changed, revoking pending approvals survives a concurrent decision, and the viewer keeps a Stop or Resume that Core did not confirm on screen with a retry. The assistant-browser-viewer spec now checks the draft-scoped session the viewer has on screen (it checked the fixture's prepared one since 5101be4) and gains a refused-Stop journey. Selected: the new Core race tests (6, all fail on main), the companion, viewer-endpoint and one-browser suites that exercise takeover, open, bind, select_tab and the tab poll, the companion stream route, the viewer component suite (5 new cases fail on main) and the assistant-browser-viewer area on its eight profiles (two journeys each).
